attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04) that survives kernel OOM events. The service (/opt/inventory-api/app.py, a threaded HTTP server on :8080 serving /health and /inventory) runs under unit inventory-api.service with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, making it effectively immune to OOM-killer selection. Verified the protection by launching a memory-hog process that exhausted the node's RAM (no swap configured): the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the memory hog (oom_score_adj:0) while inventory-api (oom_score_adj:-1000) was never touched and kept serving requests throughout. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on node1: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, issued a native `systemctl reboot`, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified inventory-api came back active/enabled with OOM protection intact and correct API responses post-recovery.
